question: What did drilling on Enewetak Atoll in 1951–52 hit beneath more than a kilometre of coral rock?
answer: Volcanic basalt. Darwin had argued in 1842 that atolls are reefs on sinking volcanoes, the coral growing upward as the peak subsided. Drill holes went through more than 1,200 m of reef limestone, tens of millions of years old, to the volcano. Surface-dwelling corals had kept pace all the way down.
move: A slow process sustained long enough builds what looks impossible.
reference: Ladd, Ingerson, Towson, Russell & Stephenson, Drilling on Eniwetok Atoll, Marshall Islands, Bulletin of the American Association of Petroleum Geologists, 1953
